asks: am I supposed to fight as azir
say: Farm behind your soldiers and scale into the team's main damage, or hold Emperor's Divide to throw a diver off you when they jump.
more: Arise! soldiers attack for you at range and hit in a line, so you deal steady damage from a spot most champions cannot reach without committing.
Early you are fragile and short on gold. With a couple of items your soldiers chew through a front line, which is why the plan is waves first and fights later.
Shifting Sands is both your escape and your engage. Dashing in and walling people into your team can win a fight outright, but leaves you with nothing if it misses.
check: Where their divers and their jungler are, and whether your dash is ready.
breaks: If you are behind and they have several divers, drop the wall play; stay behind your front line and only hit whoever walks into your soldiers.

when: you just finished your first item
asks: when am I strong as Azir
when do my soldiers start hurting
say: Your first finished item is when soldiers start to hurt, so contest the next objective, or keep farming to the second if you're behind.
more: Before that item you mostly hold the lane. After it, a soldier standing on an objective pit or a choke makes it expensive for them to walk in.
Level six is a safety spike more than a kill spike: Emperor's Divide knocks divers back, so ganks and all-ins on you get much harder.
Each item after that widens the gap. If you are even at two items, you are usually the bigger threat in a front-to-back fight.
check: How many items their mid and their divers have compared to you, and who has ultimates up.
breaks: If their team is built to jump your back line and is ahead, the item alone is not enough; fight only with your wall up and a front liner beside you.

asks: how do I trade as Azir
how do I poke with soldiers
how do I win lane on azir
say: Put a soldier on the wave and hit them when they walk up to last hit, or send it at them with Conquering Sands.
more: A soldier next to their minions makes them choose between the last hit and their health. You keep farming while they decide.
Conquering Sands moves every soldier and slows for a second, which is enough to land a few more soldier attacks before they back off.
Soldiers and sands both cost mana, so poke in bursts and keep enough to dash away with Shifting Sands if their jungler appears.
check: Your mana, whether their gap closer was just used, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: Against an assassin who can jump you once the soldier is far forward, keep the soldier close to you and just farm; trade only after their dash is used.

asks: what do I do in fights as Azir
who do I hit as azir
when do I use my ult in a fight
say: Set soldiers on their front line and hit whoever's closest, keeping the wall for a diver, or dash in with it if they clump.
more: Soldier attacks hit in a line, so placing them where their team has to stand, like a choke or a pit entrance, hits several people at once.
Emperor's Divide knocks enemies back, and the wall then stands between you and them. Used on a diver it saves you; used on a clump it starts the fight for your team.
The engage version gives up your own protection. Do it when your team is ready to follow, not as a way to start a fight alone.
check: Whether their divers have used their dashes, and whether your team is close enough to follow an engage.
breaks: If their assassin is still unseen, do not spend the wall or the dash forward; keep both until he shows, then fight normally.

when: you are behind your lane opponent in CS or kills before 14:00
asks: I'm losing lane as Azir what now
how do I come back on azir
say: You outscale most mids, so skip the trades and take every wave you safely can, or shove and recall if you can't hold lane.
more: Your value comes from items, not from winning lane. Losing some health to keep the wave coming is fine; dying for it is not.
Soldiers let you last hit and clear from behind your minions, so you can farm under pressure where a melee mid could not.
Later, Shurima's Legacy lets you raise a Disc of the Sun on turret ruins, which helps you hold a lane or keep a siege going.
check: Whether the wave is safe to walk up to, and whether their jungler and mid are both missing.
breaks: If they are diving you under tower repeatedly, farming alone will not fix it; ask for your jungler to hold mid or give the outer tower and farm the next one.

asks: what does Mundo want to do
say: Farm through the early levels and become the tank they can't kill, or throw Infected Bonesaw from range when walking up costs too much.
more: Blunt Force Trauma gives you attack damage from your maximum health, so health items make you both harder to kill and more dangerous.
Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilizing effect that hits you. Their one stun often does nothing, which is why you can simply walk at people later.
Early you have little kill pressure. The lane is about last hits and staying healthy, not about winning trades.
check: Whether your passive is up before you walk into their crowd control.
breaks: If they have several immobilizing spells in a row, the passive only eats the first; wait for your team to go in with you instead of running in alone.

when: you just reached level 6
asks: can I fight now I have ult
what does my ult do for me
say: Maximum Dosage at six heals back a bad trade, so you can stay and farm, or run them down with its speed if they're low.
more: The ultimate heals part of your missing health at once and keeps regenerating for a long time, so it is strongest when used while you are already hurt.
It also gives move speed. That lets you chase a low laner, reach a carry later, or simply leave a gank.
Your bigger spikes are finished health items. Each one raises the heal, your attack damage and how long you can stand in a fight.
check: Their health, and whether they have a way to cut healing or burst you before the regeneration matters.
breaks: If their jungler is likely nearby, keep the ultimate for him; a gank you walk away from is worth more than one aggressive trade.

asks: how do I trade as Mundo
should I fight him in lane
how do I lane on mundo
do I throw cleavers or walk up
say: Slow them with Bonesaw first, then walk in with Heart Zapper and Blunt Force Trauma, or just bonesaw the wave if they win close.
more: Infected Bonesaw deals damage based on their current health, so it does the most to a full-health opponent and is your safest way to start.
Heart Zapper stores part of the damage you take and bursts at the end, so turn it on when they commit to hitting you back.
Blunt Force Trauma hits harder the more health you are missing. A trade you looked like losing can flip on that last hit.
check: Whether minions are in the way of the bonesaw, and how big their wave is when you walk in.
breaks: If they out-damage you up close at this stage, do not walk in at all; last hit with the bonesaw from range and wait for health items.

asks: what do I do in fights as Mundo
who do I go on as mundo
say: Use Maximum Dosage and run at their carries so they must deal with you, or guard your own carry if you're the only tank.
more: You have no hard crowd control, only the bonesaw slow. Your threat is that you keep walking and keep hitting, so the fight bends around you.
Your passive shrugging off the first immobilize means you often reach the back line when another tank would be stopped at the front.
If you are the only front liner, chasing deep leaves your carries alone. Staying near them and hitting whoever dives is the safer version.
check: Whether your team is close enough to follow you, and whether your passive is up.
breaks: If they have strong healing reduction and percent-health damage and you are not ahead, do not dive alone; go in second, after their main spells are used.

when: you are behind your lane opponent in CS or kills before 14:00
asks: I'm behind on Mundo what do I do
how do I come back as mundo
do I just farm under tower
say: Health items fix a bad lane for you, so farm near your tower with Bonesaw, or use Maximum Dosage to stay through one more wave.
more: You do not need to win lane. You need last hits, and the bonesaw gets them from a distance even when you cannot walk up.
Every wave you catch brings the point closer where their damage stops being enough. Dying for a wave pushes that point further away.
Once you have an item or two, group for the next objective. A tank who turns up is worth more than one still fixing a lost lane.
check: Whether the wave is close enough to farm safely, and whether their jungler is on your side of the map.
breaks: If they are freezing the wave far from your tower, the bonesaw is not enough; ask your jungler to help break it, or take a nearby camp between waves.

asks: am I a ganker on graves
say: You're a farming carry: clear fast, take their camps and win duels, or gank only when the lane brings the crowd control.
more: New Destiny fires four pellets that cannot pass through units, so you hit hardest up close on one target, which is why you duel well in the jungle.
Quickdraw gives armor and magic resist, and dashing toward a champion gives more. You are tankier in a fight than a normal marksman, as long as you keep dashing.
You carry by being a level and an item ahead of their jungler. Gold from camps matters more to you than a risky early gank.
check: Whether their jungler is someone you can duel at this point, and whether your lanes can move to help you.
breaks: If your lanes are all losing and cannot follow you into their jungle, stop invading; farm your own side and gank the one lane that can set you up.

when: before 3:30
asks: what's my first clear as Graves
how should I path on graves
say: Full clear all six camps to about level four and reach a crab healthy, or stop at three and invade if their jungler's weaker early.
more: Your pellets knock back small monsters hit by several at once, so camps spend less time hitting you. That keeps you healthy through a full clear.
Pellets cannot pass through units, so stand where the big monster is not hidden behind the small ones. End of the Line detonates on terrain, so fire it into a wall.
Finishing at level four near a crab, which spawns at 2:55, sets up your second clear and a fight for river control while you are strong.
check: Which side your stronger lanes are on, and whether their jungler showed on the map during your clear.
breaks: If their jungler is a strong early ganker and your lanes are pushed up, the greedy full clear costs a lane; warn them, or finish on the side he is likely to hit.

asks: who do I gank as Graves
is this a good gank for graves
say: Gank lanes that have a stun or root to start it, or take their camps instead while their jungler is showing on the other side.
more: Your only crowd control is the brief slow from Smoke Screen. Without a lane stun, most targets simply walk away and you lose camp time.
Minions block your pellets, so come from an angle where the wave is not between you and the target.
When no lane is gankable, a stolen camp is the same gold with none of the risk, and it sets their jungler behind for the next objective.
check: Whether your laner's crowd control is ready, where the wave is, and whether the target still has an escape.
breaks: If a lane is being dived and needs you, go even without a perfect setup; holding a tower and saving a death beats the extra camp.

when: you reached level 6 or just finished your first item
asks: can I fight their jungler now
am I strong enough to invade
say: First item and level six is your duel window, so look for their jungler in river, or take his far-side camps while he ganks.
more: Collateral Damage deals heavy damage to the first champion it hits, so open with attacks and use it to finish a short duel.
The first finished damage item is where your pellets up close start to out-trade most junglers. If the feed shows you a level up as well, press it.
Used on camps, the same lead grows quietly. Used on a river fight before a dragon or the grubs at 8:00, it wins the objective.
check: His level and items compared to yours, and whether his lanes can reach the fight before yours.
breaks: If he is a tank with lockdown and his laners have priority, the duel is a trap; take camps across the map from him instead.

asks: what do I do in fights as Graves
who do I shoot as graves
do I flank or front line
should I go for their adc
say: Shoot whoever is closest and keep dashing for armor, or flank with Smoke Screen and Collateral Damage if their carry stands alone.
more: Because units block your pellets, you usually cannot reach a back line through a front line. Hitting the nearest target hard is the reliable job.
Smoke Screen cuts sight range for enemies inside it. Dropped on a marksman or mage, it stops them finding targets for a moment.
The flank is higher reward but you are short ranged. It works when their carry has no protector nearby, and fails badly when one is waiting.
check: Who is standing next to their carry, and whether your Quickdraw is up before you step in.
breaks: If you are the only real damage on your team, do not flank at all; stay with your front line and stay alive for the whole fight.

asks: am I a tank or a fighter
say: Play as a tank who locks people down and guards carries, or use All Out to pull one target away and kill it alone.
more: Outside the ultimate you are a durable front liner with a pull, a stun and a shield you can share with an ally.
All Out trades your defenses for damage and healing. It turns you into a duelist for one fight, which is strong on an isolated target and risky with their team nearby.
Early you want a steady lane. Your value climbs as fights start around objectives, where both halves of the kit matter.
check: How many enemies are near the target you want to knock away, and whether your team needs a front line more.
breaks: If you are your team's only tank, going All Out removes the front line; keep it for a clear kill or to end a fight that is already won.

when: you just reached level 6
asks: can I kill him at six
is my ult a big deal
say: At six All Out can knock them through a wall into a duel, or hold it, because you give up defenses to use it.
more: The knockback launches them through any wall in the path, so it can take a laner away from their tower or away from help.
While All Out you deal more damage and heal, your dash and strikes come back faster, but Path Maker no longer stuns. Land the crowd control before you transform.
Held, it is a strong answer to a gank: knock one of them away through a wall and fight the other.
check: Their health, which wall is behind them, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If their jungler is near or they out-damage you in a straight fight, do not transform; stay a tank and trade with the pull and stun.

asks: how do I trade as K'Sante
how do I lane on ksante
say: Land two Ntofo Strikes on anything, pull them in with the third and hit once, or keep it for farming when they out-trade you.
more: Two stacks of Ntofo Strikes turn the next one into a shockwave that pulls. You can build the stacks on minions and save the pull for the champion.
Your abilities mark targets so the next attack hurts more. Ability, then one attack, then step back is a full trade.
Footwork gives a shield, so use it as they hit back. Path Maker reduces damage while charging, which blunts their biggest spell.
check: Your mana, the size of their wave, and whether they have a dash to dodge the pull.
breaks: If they are ranged and never let you stack, do not chase; farm with the strikes and trade only when they step up for a last hit.

asks: what do I do in fights as K'Sante
say: Front line with Path Maker and shield your carry with Footwork, or knock their carry through a wall when your team can follow.
more: Path Maker's dash knocks back and stuns, and Footwork can dash to an ally so you both get a shield. That is real protection for a carry.
All Out removes one enemy from the fight for a moment, and you with them. That is great on their main damage, and poor if your team loses without you.
Which one is right depends on who is the bigger threat: their diver, or their back line.
check: Whether their divers have already gone in, and whether your team can win the rest of the fight while you are away.
breaks: If their team has more crowd control than yours can survive, stay as the tank all fight; a dead carry behind you is worse than a missed pick.

when: your lane opponent is a ranged champion
asks: how do I lane against ranged as K'Sante
what do I do against this poke
say: Charge Path Maker through the poke to reach them when they step up, or give some farm and wait for six or your jungler.
more: Path Maker reduces the damage you take while it charges, so you can walk through one round of poke and still land the stun.
Footwork's shield covers the walk back. One good stun into a pull is often enough to make them respect the wave.
If it is not working, losing some last hits is acceptable. You stay useful as a tank even from behind, and a death is what really sets you back.
check: Your health and mana, and whether they have a dash that makes the charge miss.
breaks: If you are too low to walk through even one round of poke, stop trying; recall on a pushed wave and come back with health.

say: You're an early assassin: win lane with Distortion trades and roam for kills, or shove and move first if your laner plays safe.
more: Distortion is a dash you can undo within a few seconds, so you can go in, deal damage and be back where you started before they answer.
Your burst is on single squishy targets. You get the most from the middle of the game, catching people who are alone.
Mirror Image makes you invisible for a moment at low health and leaves a copy, which often buys the second you need to escape.
check: Who on their team is squishy and walking alone, and where their crowd control is.
breaks: If they group tightly with tanks in front, picks dry up; poke from range with Sigil of Malice and wait for someone to step out.

when: you just reached level 6
asks: can I kill him at six
what do I copy with ult
say: Mimic at six repeats one basic spell, so look for a kill mid or on a side lane, or copy Distortion to escape.
more: A second Sigil of Malice or a second Distortion is what turns your trade into a kill on a squishy target.
Copying Ethereal Chains gives a second chance at the root. Copying Distortion gives a second dash, which makes ganks on you very hard.
If the feed shows you reached six before their mid, that gap is your best moment in the lane.
check: Their health, whether their defensive spell or summoner is up, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If they are a tanky mid or already hold a defensive item, the solo kill is unlikely; shove the wave and take the spike to a side lane.

asks: how do I trade as LeBlanc
how do I poke as lb
say: Mark them with Sigil of Malice, dash on with Distortion to pop it and snap back, or just Sigil when their stun is up.
more: The sigil's mark detonates when another ability hits, so Sigil then Distortion is two hits of damage in one short trade.
You can return to where you started for a few seconds after dashing. Go back before their answer lands rather than staying to attack.
Ethereal Chains roots only if they stay shackled for a second and a half, so throw it when they have nowhere to walk.
check: Your mana, whether their crowd control is ready, and whether minions block the chain.
breaks: If they hold a stun for the moment you land, dashing in gets you caught; poke with the sigil alone and wait for the stun to be used.

when: their mid laner is dead and you are level 6 or higher
asks: where do I go as LeBlanc now
do I roam bot or top
say: With their mid dead, push the wave in and walk to a side lane for a pick, or take their raptors if both lanes play back.
more: Pushing first means your tower loses nothing and their mid comes back to a wave under tower instead of following you.
Distortion gets you over a wall into a lane quickly, and Mimic gives a second spell to finish. Lanes with crowd control of their own are the best targets.
If neither lane is gankable, enemy camps or deep vision still turn the free time into something.
check: Which side lane has an enemy pushed up and low, and how long is left on their mid's respawn.
breaks: If your own wave is about to crash into your tower, catch it first; a roam that finds nothing and costs two waves is a loss.

asks: what do I do in fights as LeBlanc
who do I go on as lb
say: Wait at the side for a squishy to step out and burst them, or chain whoever dives your carry if no pick is there.
more: You do one target's worth of damage, then wait. Spending it on a tank at the front wastes the fight.
Distortion in and back lets you test their back line: if the burst kills, good, and if not you are back out before they turn.
Ethereal Chains on a diver is real peel. It is less exciting than a pick, but it keeps your main damage alive.
check: Where their carry is standing, and which of their crowd control spells have been used.
breaks: If their back line is guarded and you are not ahead, forget the dive; poke with the sigil before the fight and play near your carry.

when: after 14:00 and you are ahead in kills
asks: how do I use my lead as LeBlanc
what now I'm fed on lb
how do I close this out
say: Spend your lead on picks before each objective so fights start uneven, or push a side lane and escape with Distortion when they come.
more: Your burst matters most while squishy targets still die to one rotation. As they finish defensive items, that window narrows.
A kill thirty seconds before dragon or baron decides it without a real fight. That is the best use of an assassin lead.
In a side lane you are hard to catch: one dash over a wall, and the ultimate can copy it for a second.
check: Which enemies are showing alone, and whether the next objective is up within a minute or so.
breaks: If they stop walking alone and group five, picks are gone; stay with your team and look for the flank once the fight has started.

say: Keep your carry alive and hitting from further away with Cozy Campfire and shields, or kick away whoever jumps on them.
more: Cozy Campfire heals and adds attack range for allies inside it, and it follows the ally nearest where you cast it. Range is the special thing you give.
Warm Hugs holds two charges, each a shield with a little move speed. Fired Up makes an ally you touch with an ability burn their next target.
You have almost no way to start a fight. Your game is making one carry much better and undoing the enemy's engage.
check: Which ally is actually dealing the damage, and where the enemy's divers are.
breaks: If your carry is far behind, attach yourself to whichever teammate is strongest instead; the range and shields work on anyone who attacks.

when: you just reached level 6

when do I use milio ult
say: Breath of Life at six strips crowd control from allies, so you can take fights into their stun, or hold it for a dive.
more: The ultimate heals and removes crowd control from allies in range. Against a lane whose kill depends on one stun or root, it cancels the kill.
It is reactive: it does the most pressed just after their crowd control lands, not before.
It also makes you a strong answer to tower dives and ganks, because the lockdown that makes those work does not last.
check: Whether their engage spell and their jungler's crowd control are ready.
breaks: If their damage is pure burst with no crowd control, the cleanse does little; use it early as a heal rather than waiting.

asks: how do I trade as Milio
how do I help my adc trade
say: Shield your carry as they step up so Fired Up burns on their next hit, or drop Campfire and out-range them instead.
more: Your abilities enchant the ally they touch, so a shield just before your carry attacks adds a burst and a burn to that attack.
Campfire's extra range lets your carry hit without being hit back. Against a shorter-ranged lane, that alone wins trades over time.
Ultra Mega Fire Kick knocks back one enemy and slows around where the ball lands. It is poke, but it is also your only disengage.
check: Your mana, and whether their engage is coming before you spend the kick on poke.
breaks: If they have an all-in waiting, do not kick for poke; hold it, keep both shields and trade only with range.

asks: what do I do in fights as Milio
who do I stand next to
when do I ult in a fight
say: Stand by your main carry with Campfire down and shields ready, or spread the ultimate over several allies if their engage hits many.
more: Campfire on the carry gives them extra range, and it follows them, so it keeps working as the fight moves.
Breath of Life is worth the most when it frees two or three allies from the same engage. Standing a little central keeps more people in range.
Keep the kick for whoever reaches your carry. A knockback on a diver at the right moment is often the whole fight.
check: Who their team is trying to dive, and whether your allies are close enough for the ultimate to reach them.
breaks: If you are the one being targeted first, stand further back and give up some range; a dead Milio protects nobody.

when: their support is an engage or hook champion
asks: how do I lane against engage as Milio
how do I stop their all in
what do I do against this lane
say: Hold Ultra Mega Fire Kick to knock the diver back, or stand behind minions and only shield trades until you're six.
more: The kick is the one spell you have that stops someone mid-engage. If it was spent on poke, their next engage is free.
Warm Hugs gives move speed as well as a shield, which helps your carry step out of the follow-up.
From six, Breath of Life removes the crowd control. That is when you can stand further up and let them try.
check: Whether their hook or engage was just used, and how many minions stand between you and them.
breaks: If they have engage plus a gank coming, no spell saves the lane; back off to your tower and let the wave come to you.

say: Control lane with the ball and scale into a teamfight mage, or put the ball on a diving ally and shockwave from them.
more: Everything you do comes from the ball, not from you. That lets you stand far back while the ball threatens the space your team wants.
Command: Protect shields an ally and carries the ball with them. A teammate who jumps in is your best way to deliver Command: Shockwave.
Early you are a safe laner with good wave clear. Your game is won in the fights around objectives later.
check: Where the ball is right now, and which ally is able to carry it into their team.
breaks: If nobody on your team can go in, do not walk forward to place the ball yourself; zone with it and use the shockwave on whoever dives.

when: you just reached level 6
asks: can we fight now I have ult
is six a big deal for ori
say: Six gives you Shockwave, so a fight at the next objective favors you if it lands, or keep farming toward your first item.
more: Command: Shockwave pulls nearby enemies toward the ball after a short delay. On two or more people in a river or pit, it decides the fight.
In lane it is a kill threat with your jungler: the ball on him as he arrives means the shockwave lands where he lands.
Your first finished item is the second half of the spike. That is where the ball starts clearing waves quickly and poke adds up.
check: Whether the enemy will be bunched at the objective, and whether your jungler is on your side of the map.
breaks: If they spread out and poke rather than group, a big shockwave will not be there; use it on one target that steps too close.

asks: how do I trade as Orianna
how do I poke with the ball
how do I win lane on ori
say: Send the ball through them and pulse Dissonance as they last hit, or keep the ball on yourself when a gank looks likely.
more: Command: Attack leaves the ball where it lands, so one cast both pokes and sets up the next. The Dissonance pulse then slows them for a follow-up.
Clockwork Windup adds magic damage to your attacks and more on repeated hits. A couple of attacks after the ball lands is a real trade early.
A ball left far forward means no shield for you. Against junglers who can reach you, bringing it home is part of trading.
check: Your mana, where the ball is sitting, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If they are an assassin waiting for the ball to be away, stop poking forward; shield yourself and clear the wave from range.

asks: what do I do in fights as Orianna
who do I put the ball on
say: Put the ball on whoever starts the fight and shockwave when they arrive, or hold it to stop a dive on your carry.
more: The engage version wins fights at once: ball on your diver, shockwave as he reaches them, then Dissonance to slow whoever is pulled in.
The defensive version keeps the ball near your carry. Whoever jumps on them gets pulled, slowed and focused.
Dissonance also speeds allies up. Laid in front of your team it helps them reach a target or get away.
check: Which of your allies is going in, and where their divers are standing before the fight starts.
breaks: If your engager is dead or far away, do not force the shockwave; play it as a zone on the choke and make them walk into it.

when: you are behind your lane opponent in CS or kills before 14:00
asks: I'm behind on Orianna what now
how do I come back as ori
say: You don't need kills, just waves: clear from range with the ball and reach two items, or shield your jungler when he plays mid.
more: The ball lets you take a wave from well behind it. Health lost to poke comes back; a death and two missed waves do not.
Even from behind, a good Shockwave at an objective is worth as much as a fed player's damage. Your fights do not depend on your lane.
Shielding a jungler who comes mid costs little and makes his gank safer, so you help without having to step up yourself.
check: Whether the wave is safe to reach, and whether their mid and jungler are both missing.
breaks: If they keep diving you under tower, farming alone will not hold; ask for help mid or give the outer tower and farm safely behind it.

say: You're a combo fighter who snowballs: take short trades and then own a side lane, or farm quietly if you fall behind.
more: Broken Wings is three strikes with a knockback on the last, Ki Burst is a stun around you and Valor is a short dash that blocks damage. Together you move a lot and trade fast.
You use no resource, so nothing but cooldowns limits how often you trade. A lane where they run short on mana tilts toward you over time.
Runic Blade adds damage to an attack after each ability, so weaving attacks between spells is where your damage comes from.
check: Whether your abilities are up before each trade, and where their jungler is.
breaks: If you are behind, the all-in stops working; trade only when they use a key spell on the wave, and wait for your team to make something happen.

when: you just reached level 6
asks: can I kill him at six
say: Six is a kill window: start Blade of the Exile early for damage and reach, then finish with Wind Slash, or hold it defensively.
more: The ultimate gives attack damage and range for its whole duration, so pressing it at the start of the fight is worth more than saving it.
Wind Slash is a single ranged attack you can use once while it is active. Keep it for the end, when they are running.
If the feed shows you hit six first, that level gap is the best moment in the lane to commit.
check: Their health, whether they have an escape or a defensive spell ready, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If they are six as well with a stronger extended fight, do not full commit; trade short with the ultimate on and back off.

asks: how do I trade as Riven
how do I win lane on riven
say: Close with Broken Wings, stun with Ki Burst and attack, then Valor out to block the return, or Valor in if they're ranged.
more: Valor's shield is what makes the trade a win. Used as they hit back, you take almost nothing and keep the health lead.
Attack after each ability so Runic Blade is not wasted. A slower combo with attacks in it beats a fast one without.
Using Valor to get in works on targets you cannot otherwise reach, but then the block is gone, so keep that trade very short.
check: The size of their minion wave, and whether their main trading spell is ready.
breaks: If they are a strong sustained fighter, stay out of long trades; hit once after they use a spell on the wave and leave.

asks: what do I do in fights as Riven
who do I go on as riven
say: Come from the side onto their back line once key spells are used, or push a side lane if they have too much lockdown.
more: Your stun hits everyone around you and your third strike knocks back, so landing in the middle of two carries is your best fight.
You are not a tank. Going in first means eating every crowd control spell they have; going in second means they have none left.
In a side lane your mobility makes you hard to catch, and drawing two people there wins the objective for the other four.
check: Which crowd control spells they have already used, and whether your team is ready to fight when you go.
breaks: If you are behind, the back line dive fails; stay near your own carry and stun whoever jumps on them instead.

when: your lane opponent is a tank
asks: how do I play Riven into a tank
what do I do against this tank
say: Win the early levels with repeated short trades before his armor comes, or shove the wave and move with your jungler.
more: Tanks are weakest before their first defensive item. Your free, resourceless trades are how you build a lead in that time.
Once the feed shows him with armor, the solo kill fades. Your lead is then better spent on plates, grubs from 8:00 or a river fight.
Later he wins by standing in front of his team. You win by being in a side lane where he has to face you alone or give the tower.
check: His health and items, and whether his crowd control is ready when you go in.
breaks: If he got ahead early, do not keep forcing; farm safely and look for fights with your team where he is not the target.

asks: am I a tank or a ganker
say: You're a ganking tank: catch one target with Ixtal's Impact or Impale and bring it to your team, or guard your carry.
more: Ixtal's Impact charges through terrain and slams a champion into the next wall for a stun. Impale suppresses and drags. Both move an enemy where you want them.
Threads of Vibration deals damage based on maximum health once stacked, so you stay useful against tanks while building tanky yourself.
You need little gold. Early ganks and being at every objective matter more than a perfect farm count.
check: Which lanes have damage to follow your catch, and where the walls are around the target.
breaks: If your team has no damage to follow up, a catch does nothing; switch to protecting whoever is carrying.

when: before 3:30
asks: what's my first clear as Skarner
do I full clear on skarner
should I gank early or farm
say: Full clear to about level four, slamming big monsters into walls with Ixtal's Impact, or take three camps and gank a pushed-up lane.
more: Ixtal's Impact works on large monsters too, stunning and damaging them against a wall. Seismic Bastion's shield keeps the clear healthy.
You lean toward ganking early. The charge comes through terrain, so you arrive from angles a lane does not expect.
A full clear ends near a crab, which spawns at 2:55. A three camp start trades that farm for an earlier gank, worth it only if the lane is really open.
check: Which lane is pushed toward the enemy tower, and whether that laner has used their escape.
breaks: If no lane is gankable after three camps, do not hover; finish the clear so you are not behind on levels at the first objective.

asks: who do I gank as Skarner
how do I gank on skarner
say: Come through a wall with Ixtal's Impact and pin them to the next one, or wait for six and drag them with Impale.
more: The charge needs a wall behind the target to stun. Lanes with walls close by, and targets standing near them, are your best ganks.
Coming through terrain skips the usual river entrance, so a lane that looks safe from the river often is not safe from you.
Before six, a missed charge is the whole gank. After six, Impale is a second way to catch, so you can gank lanes with escapes.
check: Where the target stands relative to walls, whether their dash is up, and whether your laner can follow.
breaks: If the target sits in open lane away from walls, the stun will not happen; pick another lane or take a camp and return.

when: you just reached level 6
asks: what do I do at six
say: Impale at six suppresses and drags whoever you catch, so gank the lane with your carry, or hold it for the dragon fight.
more: A suppressed target is dragged along as you move, so you can pull them out from under their tower or into your team.
It can catch more than one champion in front of you. In a river choke before an objective, that can start the fight two players up.
Using it on a lane now builds a lead. Holding it means the next objective fight starts on your terms.
check: Whether the next dragon or the grubs are about to be contested, and which ally is close enough to kill the target.
breaks: If the only target is a tank with nobody near to hurt him, do not spend it; wait for a carry to step into range.

asks: what do I do in fights as Skarner
when do I ult in a fight
say: Start the fight by dragging whoever you reach into your team with Impale, or stay back and impale whoever dives your carry.
more: Ixtal's Impact through a wall gets you onto their flank, and Impale brings the catch back. That is your engage.
Seismic Bastion shields you and slows around you, so once you are in the middle you stay a problem for a while.
The peel version is less dramatic but sure. A suppressed diver deals no damage, and your carry gets free time.
check: Whether their carry is reachable, and whether your own carry is the one in danger.
breaks: If they have several divers and your carry is your only damage, do not go looking for the engage; stand next to the carry all fight.

say: You win one-on-one fights and take towers quickly, so push a side lane, or steal a tank's stats with Subjugate in team fights.
more: Frozen Domain gives attack speed, move speed and extra healing while you stand on it. Fights and towers on your own ground go much faster.
Chomp takes some of the target's attack damage, and King's Tribute heals you when nearby enemies die. You are built for long fights near minions or monsters.
Pillar of Ice makes a wall that slows. It is your only crowd control, and it both starts chases and blocks escapes.
check: Who would have to answer you in a side lane, and whether they can beat you alone.
breaks: If they have ranged champions who never let you reach them, the duel plan fails; stay with your team and use the pillar and ultimate for them.

when: before 3:30
asks: what's my first clear as Trundle
do I full clear on trundle
say: King's Tribute heals as monsters die, so full clear healthy to level four, or invade at three since you duel well early.
more: Fighting camps on Frozen Domain speeds up every attack and boosts your healing, so you finish a clear with health to spare.
That health is the point. Arriving at the 2:55 crab or in their jungle nearly full, against a jungler who is not, is how you get ahead.
You are happy either farming or fighting early. What you want to avoid is long ganks on lanes that have no setup.
check: Whether their jungler is weak in early duels, and whether your nearest laners can move if a fight starts.
breaks: If their mid and side lane have priority near the invade, you get collapsed on; stay on your own side and meet him at the crab instead.

asks: who do I gank as Trundle
how do I gank on trundle
say: Gank lanes where Pillar of Ice can block their way out, or skip it and fight their jungler at the crab instead.
more: The pillar is impassable and slows everything near it. Placed behind a target, or in a narrow part of lane, it turns a walk away into a kill.
Chomp adds a brief slow and cuts their attack damage, so once you reach someone they struggle to fight back.
With one piece of crowd control, a gank on a target with a dash is a coin flip. A river duel is often the more reliable use of that time.
check: Whether the target has a dash that goes around the pillar, and how far up the lane they are.
breaks: If your laner is too low to follow, do not gank; cover the wave so they can recall, then return to your camps.

when: you just reached level 6
asks: can I fight their tank now
what does six do for me
say: Six is strongest into tanks: Subjugate takes their health and resistances, so fight their front liner, or keep it for a dive on you.
more: Subjugate steals a share of health, armor and magic resist at once and more over the next four seconds. The tankier the target, the more you gain.
Against a tank laner or jungler it flips a duel that was even. Against a squishy it is mostly a heal.
Defensively it is the same button: pressed on the biggest enemy when you are dived, you get harder to kill while they get softer.
check: Which enemy has the most health and resistances, and whether you can stay on them for the full effect.
breaks: If their team has no real tank, the ultimate is only a heal; rely on Frozen Domain and Chomp for your fights instead.

when: your lane opponent is a melee attack damage fighter
asks: how do I lane as Trundle
can I fight him as trundle
how do I trade on trundle
say: Chomp cuts their attack damage, so trade when they walk onto your Frozen Domain, or farm and heal off the dying wave.
more: A fighter who relies on attack damage loses part of it for a moment after Chomp, while you attack faster on your ground.
King's Tribute heals you as minions die nearby. Simply being near a dying wave undoes a lot of their poke.
Pillar of Ice behind them as they retreat extends the trade by a few attacks, and that is usually where you pull ahead.
check: Whether Frozen Domain is under the fight, and whether their big cooldown is ready.
breaks: If they are ranged or deal magic damage, Chomp's cut matters far less; take short trades and lean on the wave healing.

asks: what do I do in fights as Trundle
who do I ult in a fight
say: Subjugate their biggest tank and pillar their carry away from the fight, or split a side lane and make them answer you.
more: Taking a tank's resistances makes him die to your team and makes you the front line in his place.
Pillar of Ice can cut a choke, separate a carry from the fight or stop an escape. One good pillar is often worth more than your damage.
The split works because few champions want to duel you on Frozen Domain. If two come, your team should start the objective.
check: Whether an objective is up for your team to take while you split, and who they send to you.
breaks: If your team cannot fight four against four without you, do not split; group, and use the pillar to protect your carry.

say: You're weak early and a monster late: farm and heal with Transfusion until items, or pool into fights your team starts.
more: Crimson Pact turns ability power into health and health into ability power, so every item makes you both tankier and stronger.
Transfusion heals you off a target, and you use no mana. You can stay in lane as long as you avoid big trades.
Late, you walk into the middle of a fight, hit everyone with Hemoplague and Tides of Blood, and sink into Sanguine Pool when they turn on you.
check: How many items you have compared to their damage dealers, and whether your team has someone to start fights.
breaks: If the game is being decided early around objectives, you cannot just farm forever; show up when you have the ultimate and stay at the edge.

asks: when can I fight as vlad
how many items do I need
say: Your real spikes are finished items, so keep farming to two, or fight at six if Hemoplague can cover several of them.
more: Hemoplague makes infected enemies take more damage for its duration. It helps your whole team, so it is best on a group, not one person.
In lane, six gives some kill threat when they are already low, but you are still fragile compared to later.
Each finished item counts twice because of Crimson Pact. The feed showing your second item done is roughly where you stop avoiding fights.
check: Whether the enemy is grouped tightly enough for the ultimate, and how your items compare to theirs.
breaks: If you are behind on items, even a good ultimate will not carry a fight; use it from the edge and leave through the pool.

asks: how do I trade as Vladimir
how do I lane on vlad
say: Trade when Transfusion is empowered, since it hits and heals much harder, or use it on minions while it charges.
more: Your resource bar fills as you use Transfusion. When it is full, the next one is far stronger for a short time, so walk up then.
Tides of Blood costs your own health and is blocked by enemy units. It is for clearing waves or hitting someone with no minions in front.
Sanguine Pool makes you untargetable for two seconds. Keep it for their biggest spell or a gank, not for extra damage.
check: Whether your resource bar is full, and whether minions stand between you and them.
breaks: If they out-range you and punish every step forward, give up trading; heal on minions with Transfusion and take what farm is safe.

asks: what do I do in fights as Vladimir
when do I go in as vlad
say: Flank in, put Hemoplague on as many as you can and release Tides of Blood, or hold Sanguine Pool for their biggest spell.
more: Your damage is around you and in an area, so you want to be among several of them, not picking at the front.
Enemy units block Tides of Blood, so a flank onto the back line, with no tanks in the way, lands far more of it.
The pool is your one escape. Using it to dodge the spell meant to kill you keeps you in the fight; using it to go in leaves you stuck.
check: Which crowd control they still hold, and whether your team is fighting at the same moment you arrive.
breaks: If you are not yet at two items, the deep flank gets you killed; stand with your team and hit whoever comes to you.

when: you are behind your lane opponent in CS or kills before 14:00
asks: I'm behind on Vlad what now
how do I come back as vladimir
say: No mana means they can't starve you out, so stay, farm and heal with Transfusion, or give the wave when their jungler's near.
more: Transfusion on a minion is a last hit and a heal together. A lane you are losing can still be a lane you farm.
You outscale most opponents once items come. Not dying is worth more to you than any single wave.
Sanguine Pool is your answer to a gank or a dive, so farming forward without it ready is the real risk.
check: Whether your pool is ready, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If they can kill you through the pool under your own tower, staying is wrong; recall, ask for cover and give up the outer tower if needed.

say: You're an assassin: poke with shurikens through your shadow, then kill a carry with Death Mark, or push a side lane when they group.
more: Living Shadow copies your abilities, so a shuriken or slash can come from two places. That is your poke, and it works from a safe distance.
Death Mark makes you untargetable as you dash on, then repeats part of the damage you dealt after three seconds. One squishy target is your whole job.
You use energy, not mana, so you never run dry in lane; you just have to wait between rotations.
check: Which enemy carry is reachable and alone, and which of their protective spells are ready.
breaks: If every carry has a protector standing by, do not force the dive; poke before fights or pull someone to a side lane.

when: you just reached level 6
asks: can I kill him at six
say: Six is your kill window: Death Mark repeats part of your damage after three seconds, so all-in, or use it to dodge their spell.
more: Everything you land in those three seconds adds to the mark. Shurikens, slash and attacks first, then the mark does the rest.
You are untargetable during the dash. Timed against their main spell, the ultimate is defense and offense together.
If the feed shows you reached six before their mid, go before they catch up. The same window works on a side lane.
check: Their health, whether they have a defensive spell, summoner or item ready, and where their jungler is.
breaks: If they hold a way to wait out the mark, bait it first with normal trades; all-in on the next rotation.

asks: how do I trade as Zed
how do I poke with shadow
should I use W to poke
say: Send Living Shadow forward and line both shurikens through them, or last hit with shuriken alone and keep your energy.
more: A shuriken from you and one from the shadow both hitting is your full poke, and landing the same ability with both gives energy back.
Shadow Slash from the shadow slows, which makes the shurikens easier to land when cast together.
Once the shadow is used you have little left to answer a gank or an all-in until it returns, so choose the moment.
check: Your energy, whether minions matter for your angle, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If they are a ranged mage who punishes every step, do not spend the shadow on poke; farm with shurikens and wait for six.

asks: what do I do in fights as Zed
who do I ult in a fight
say: Wait at the side until their key spells are used, then Death Mark the carry, or split a side lane if they're protected.
more: Going in first means every crowd control spell lands on you. Going in late means the carry is already busy and has nothing left.
One dead carry at the start of your team's push usually decides the fight. You do not need to do anything else.
In a side lane you clear waves quickly with shurikens and are hard to pin down, so you draw people away from the objective.
check: Which protective spells and items their carry still has, and whether your team is already fighting.
breaks: If you are behind, the carry survives the mark; poke with shadows from range and go only on someone already hurt.

when: their mid laner has completed an armor item
asks: he built armor what do I do
I can't kill him anymore as Zed
how do I play lane now
say: With armor on them the solo kill gets harder, so shove and roam to side lanes, or keep poking with shurikens until they're low.
more: Your damage is physical, so an early armor item takes a real bite out of the all-in. It also costs them damage, which makes it easier to push them in.
Their side lanes did not buy armor. A wave shoved into their tower gives you time to find a kill somewhere else.
Staying to poke still works, it is just slower. Use the ultimate only once the shurikens have done most of the work.
check: Whether the wave is pushed before you leave, and which side lane has an enemy overextended.
breaks: If your side lanes are losing and pushed under tower, a roam finds nothing; stay, keep the farm lead and punish their weaker damage.

when: after 14:00 and you are ahead in kills
asks: how do I use my lead as Zed
I'm fed on zed what now
how do I end as zed
say: Use the lead now: kill whoever shows alone before each objective, or push a side lane deep and make two of them come.
more: Assassin leads fade as carries finish defensive items and teams group. The sooner the lead becomes towers and objectives, the better.
A carry dead before dragon or baron means your team takes it without a fight. Watch the respawn timers the feed gives you.
Splitting works when you can kill the one person sent to stop you. If they send two, your team should be starting something elsewhere.
check: Who is showing alone on the map, and whether an objective is about to come up.
breaks: If they stop showing alone and you cannot reach the carry in a grouped fight, stay with your team and wait for the fight to break open.
